A nurse formerly employed with Gold Coast Health has been charged with 12 offences allegedly involving six teenage girls.

Derek Jackson, who allegedly stalked and sexually abused the girls over a four-year period, was suspended in September 2025 when police launched an investigation.

The 58-year-old has been remanded in custody to face court again in July, after being refused bail on Monday.

A Gold Coast nurse who allegedly abused his position in a youth mental health ward to stalk and sexually abuse teenage girls has been refused bail by a Queensland court.

Derek George Jackson, 58, faced Southport Magistrates Court today via watchhouse video link charged with 12 offences allegedly committed against six teenage girls between November 2020 and May 2024.

Mr Jackson was arrested and charged on Saturday night with six counts of stalking, two counts of indecent treatment of a child, and one count each of sexual assault, abuse of office, possessing child exploitation material, and creating child exploitation material.

The court heard Mr Jackson was arrested in the international departures lounge of Brisbane Airport.

Magistrate Nerida Wilson said Mr Jackson told police he was travelling to Asia for dental work and intended to return to Australia in July but did not yet have a return flight booked.

The court heard Mr Jackson had been suspended from his role at Gold Coast Health since September 2025 when the police investigation into his alleged offences commenced.

Adolescent inpatients with complex mental health concerns are treated at Robina Hospital. (ABC News: Chris Gillette)

Police prosecutor Jacinta Raven told the court, Mr Jackson had been the subject of several complaints from the family of children treated through Gold Coast Health's Child and Youth Mental Health Service (CYMHS) and from staff within the service.

Ms Raven told the court Mr Jackson targeted vulnerable children who were unable to remove themselves from his presence because they were admitted to a mental health facility.

Ms Raven told the court two children had complained of inappropriate "stroking or touching of the feet or the legs" and data obtained from Mr Jackson's mobile phone appeared to show he had a "foot fetish".

She said further data from Mr Jackson's phone showed he had searched the names of several children involved in the investigation of his alleged offences, as well as some of their siblings.

"He's also searched how to delete the cache on his iPhone, and that would give the court some concern," Ms Raven said.

In considering Mr Jackson's bail, Magistrate Nerida Wilson told the court his alleged victims were compromised by malnutrition.

"[They] were often undergoing re-feeding to restore weight and overall health," Ms Wilson said.

"Many of the children were also experiencing acute mental health crises including suicidal ideations, serious self-harm episodes and suicide attempts.

"These offences occur against the most vulnerable youth within our society, including those with serious mental health issues and disorders."

Giaan Ramsay, who took her own life in July 2025, is one of six teenage girls Mr Jackson allegedly offended against. (Supplied: Steve Ramsay)

Among the six alleged victims named during Mr Jackson's court appearance was Giaan Ramsay, whose death by suicide in July 2025 sparked a Queensland Health investigation.

Police allege Mr Jackson unlawfully stalked, intimidated, harassed or abused Giaan between June 2023 and May 2024.

Ms Wilson denied Mr Jackson's application for bail on the grounds that he was an unacceptable risk of reoffending and of attempting to flee the jurisdiction.

"The court is deeply troubled by the offences before the court," Ms Wilson said.

A Gold Coast Health spokesperson said in a statement it was aware of the "concerning" allegations involving a staff member.

"Immediate measures were taken, including contacting Queensland Police Service (QPS) and removing the employee from the workplace when this was brought to our attention," the spokesperson said.

"As a values-led organisation, staff and patient safety is of the utmost importance to us, and we take these matters extremely seriously.

"We will continue to cooperate with QPS as this matter progresses."

The head of the Gold Coast Vulnerable Persons Group, Detective Inspector Paul Fletcher, said no further victims had been identified.

Paul Fletcher said police were not aware of alleged offending beyond that related to the six teenagers. (ABC Gold Coast: Danielle Mahe)

"Obviously, it's deeply concerning that people are having contact with children, especially highly vulnerable people and children in a hospital setting," he said.

"Hence when these allegations came to light they were vigorously investigated straight away."

In a statement, Queensland Health Minister Tim Nicholls said the safety and wellbeing of patients and staff was the organisation's highest priority.

"These allegations are shocking and deeply concerning," Mr Nicholls said.

"As the matter is before the courts, it would be inappropriate to comment further."

Mr Jackson has been remanded in custody to face court again next month.

Investigations are ongoing, with detectives appealing for anyone with information to come forward.
